nodes.label: Lapidary — Visual Index With A Return Path
nodes.rationale: Not a CAD editor, not a slicer, not a PDM system: the layer that makes parts you already have findable, inspectable and reachable from the tools you already use, with the edit coming back versioned.

nodes.label: Three Services, Split By Port
nodes.rationale: 3000 web (SPA, proxies /api to api:8080 and nothing else), 8080 api (grid, open path, scan trigger), 8081 worker (the directory walk and everything that touches a file). A route only the worker serves is a route no browser can reach, and the api container mounts no ingest directory to walk.

nodes.label: Scan Enqueues A Job, Never Walks In The Request
nodes.rationale: Both ports accept POST /api/libraries/{id}/scan and neither walks a directory in the request: the route writes one scan_directory job, the worker walks the mount and enqueues one job per model into the same batch, so either port's batch id reports the whole scan. Enqueueing is a database write the api may do; walking a mount and parsing geometry is not.

nodes.label: Scanning Is Idempotent
nodes.rationale: BLAKE3 is computed before anything else and a hash already in the blob store short-circuits the pipeline — no parse, no raster, no write. A second scan settles every file as skipped, which the grid reports as '6 already here'.

nodes.label: Bundled Example Parts
nodes.rationale: A DN40 flange, module-2 spur gear, vee block, mounting plate, hex spacer and idler pulley, modelled to real dimensions by example/parts/generate.py (stdlib Python, deterministic, watertight) which is committed so the STLs have a source rather than being opaque binaries. First run shows a populated grid rather than an empty one.

nodes.label: SSE Stream Over A One-Second Poll
nodes.rationale: Progress streams over SSE because a browser holds an EventSource open on a hidden document where it will not run a poll. The timer underneath is kept deliberately: the poll makes delivery correct, the stream makes it prompt.

nodes.label: cargo tree Proof That api Does Not Link The Kernel
nodes.rationale: `cargo tree -p lapidary-server | grep lapidary-cad` finds nothing; adding --features mock-kernel finds two lines. One Containerfile builds both images and compose passes SERVER_FEATURES only to worker, so the api container does not merely decline to serve /scan — the code behind it is not linked into the binary.
